card.name: Final pieces of drug names in interaction text
card.fires_on: The last piece of a drug name that is split into parts, such as -ir in acyclovir, -iren in aliskiren, -ab in trastuzumab and -ib in neratinib. It appears in interaction warnings naming a second drug.

modes.label: Ending of a drug name
modes.description: Final piece of a split drug name, mostly in a warning not to combine it with another drug.
modes.example: Do not co-administer alisk<<iren>> with candesartan cilex

modes.label: Middle of a drug class name
modes.description: Partway through a drug class name such as thiazolidinedione.
modes.example: When a thiaz<<olid>>inedione is added to glyburide

modes.label: Unit after a number
modes.description: The unit mg after a number in a range of amounts.
modes.example: equivalent to 372<< mg>> to 465 mg elemental phosph

card.plain: It marks the end of a drug name in a sentence about drugs that interact with each other.
